findings.text: A fresh address range object can be initialized empty and bound to a caller supplied address space, receiving a default operations anchor, an empty anonymous linkage and a newly initialized area lock. Lock setup has distinct variants for builds with and without area locking.

Flag state supports full initialization and wholesale replacement from a historic word value, always beginning from an all clear condition. A second reset path writes the first storage word with single update semantics and copies any remaining words with ordinary semantics.
An area supports incremental flag updates that add a set of bits, remove a set of bits, or apply both an addition set and a removal set together in one combined update.

Wholesale flag replacement requires the caller to already hold write protection on the area, while add, remove and combined updates obtain write protection on entry. Obtaining write protection does nothing when it is already held, and does nothing at all in builds without area locks.

Atomic flag access requires a stabilized area. With area locks, stabilization is provided by an address space lock owned by the caller or by the area lock itself, with an approximate address space check when precise ownership tracking is unavailable. Without area locks, holding the address space lock alone stabilizes.

Flags are stored as a fixed width bitmap where the first machine word holds the historic word value. Supported bitmap style operations include population count, intersection, union, removal, symmetric difference, equality between pairs and against a mask, subset test, any match, all match and single mask match.
Flag collections can be assembled from individual bits or by merging whole masks, either starting from an empty collection or extending an existing one.

Live areas and area descriptors provide matching conveniences for flag inspection and mutation, covering single bit test, any match, all match, single mask match, union style addition and removal style clearing.

Only a narrow allowlist of bits may use the atomic set and test paths, with other bits causing a one time warning and refusal. Requesting soft dirty tracking where the page table layer lacks support also causes a one time warning. Supplying a multi bit mask to the single mask test causes a warning.

Attachment state is held in a reference count that reads as zero while detached and one once attached. Builds without area locking always report attached and treat attachment assertions and transitions as empty.

An area starts detached, is checked for detached state before installation, and becomes attached at the moment it is installed into the address space index, after which it is visible to ordered traversal.

Read only classifications derive from boundaries, ownership and flags. Overlap with the initial break interval marks the initial heap, coverage of the recorded stack origin marks the initial stack, missing or mismatched ownership marks foreign, presence of access bits marks accessible, joint shared and writable marks shared maywrite, and upward or downward growth capability marks growable, with a partially configured growable area marking a temporary stack. Removing the operations anchor marks an area or descriptor anonymous. Effective page size uses an operations hook when available and otherwise equals the base page size. Shared memory tests are constantly negative in this configuration.

Ordered traversal over the address space index offers bounded search below a limit, forward advance, range limited forward advance, backward advance, repositioning to an address, cursor pause and cursor release, with loop helpers for full and bounded scans. Index maintenance offers clearing an interval with allocation context and installing an area over its own span while marking it attached, with allocation failure reported distinctly from success.
The transition to attached requires the caller to already hold write protection on the area and to present an area that is currently detached.

Large compound ordering metadata can be returned to order zero. A page reference is taken only when the current count is nonzero, with a null result on failure. Mapping counts add one to the stored value, using dedicated large counters for compound objects and suppressing type tagged values for small pages, and an object counts as mapped from a count of one upward. Virtual addresses convert to a compound head or owning compound object through the base page translation, and effective page shift is base shift plus compound order.
Region overlap is reported with three ordered values meaning intersects, disjoint and mixed.
A TLB flush request for an area pairs the owning address space with the area flag word.
In this configuration the tests for vmalloc and module addresses are constantly negative.
Order reset on a non large object warns once and changes nothing. Interval clear and bulk install can fail for lack of memory, which the caller must handle. Marking an already attached area warns.
